svg.title: One-degree directional tests and finite operator comparisons
svg.desc: The ordered inverse time is s plus the spatial Euler operator plus d, divided by sigma, where d=N minus one. The holomorphic halfspace test is a nonzero quotient in degree one; differentiation is invertible there. On tested coefficient complexes concentrated in degree one, equivariance for every selected algebra generator gives a genuine module-derived comparison by good truncation. This equivariance is a premise for general operator entries. The time derivative and its inverse satisfy it.
svg.text: One-degree tests and finite operator comparisons
Ordered inverse · exact halfspace quotient · a stated generator-equivariance condition
1. The inverse retains its dimension correction
ρ(s) = t + Ex τ−1 ; Ex = Σ xi ξi
φ(t) = s + (Ey + d) σ−1 ; d = N − 1
ρ(Ey) = −(Ex + d)
Without d / σ, the forward image of the proposed inverse is t − d / τ.
The principal contact coordinates do not see this order-minus-one error.
Every generator relation and both inverses: PDT.1–PDT.7, PDT.26–PDT.27.
2. The holomorphic directional coefficient has one degree
Tp(O) ≃ Vp[−1] ; Hk = 0 for k ≠ 1
Vp = colim O(B ∩ {Re t < 0}) / O(B)
Dt : Vp → Vp is an isomorphism.
Ordinary holomorphic germs still have a nonzero derivative kernel.
Exact support test, quotient and primitive: PDT.8–PDT.14.
3. Check the selected actions before taking the module roof
Premise: every selected generator satisfies
H1(α) zi = zi H1(α) ; i = 1,…,m
The induced isomorphism is A-linear on the entire tested complexes.
Finite Hom retains all cohomology, maps and homotopies.
Proved actual actions: Ds ↔ Dt and their inverses.
Strictification and its precise remaining scope: PDT.15–PDT.25, PDT.30.
